findings.evidence: Criterion c1: the packet's value-scale summary (SOURCE 7) reports 23 served peak_fraction values, lowest 4.109999999999999 and highest 11.3. The row's scoring.metric explains values are stored ×100 as percentages (leaderboard peak_fraction 0.0411..0.1130 → 4.11..11.30), so these are exactly the served scale. The row's upper range bound is null, i.e. the row declines to claim an upper bound; per the criterion an unbounded bound is never contradicted by served values, and the lower bound 0 is not contradicted by any served value (min 4.11 > 0). Unit 'percent of roofline' and range [0,null] agree with the scale the board is served on; no c1 range/unit mismatch.
findings.repair: None required on the [0,null] bound itself. Residual mismatch risk is limited to the methodology identity in f2.

uncertainties: Self-execution limits: I cannot recompute row/artifact SHA-256 hashes, fetch URLs, or run the owner's transport/qualification checks; I rely on the supplied owner-computed hashes and receipts and treat hash/transport/qualification as owner-executed, per instructions.

The packet is an exact field projection: only rows' claimed fields plus leaderboard/SPEC excerpts are supplied; unrelated response fields are not required to compare these fields, and the excerpted sources may omit context outside the excerpt bounds.

SOURCE 6 activity summary is a generated comparison, not maintainer text; per c1/c2 it settles only status evidence (nonzero added values support status 'active'), never methodology, task set, harness, judges or version identity.

SOURCE 7 value-scale summary is a generated read of the capture, not maintainer text; per c1 it can settle only whether unit/range match the served scale, never what the metric means or how it is computed.

The 'Peak fraction of problem 01's own ceiling' wording is a registry/row text choice; the SPEC.md roofline for 01 is consistent with it but SPEC.md does not define a numeric ceiling value, so I treat the phrasing as not contradicted rather than verified numerically.

Opus 5 04 value 1.961 = 196.1% > 100% is consistent with the row's claim that values above 100% are possible; I treat this as consistent, not as independent confirmation of the ×100 storage convention beyond SOURCE 7's scale summary.
F2 repair requires the producer to either amend wording or supply the affected row; until then the mismatch risk is unresolved on methodology identity, driving the 'revise' verdict.
